title: Change who signs in with a connection
summary: The caution confirmation an operator gets on Lakeside University's page after picking 'Operators' under 'Who signs in with it': the 88 customer accounts go back to email codes and passkeys, product cards stop routing its domains, DJDL's Access rule narrows, and nobody gains console access.
compare: Opened by picking a different 'Who signs in with it' card on identity.connection; the selection stays on Customers (the picked card shows focus only) until the dialog is confirmed. Escape and Cancel change nothing.

An L1 caution confirm (ADMIN.md §5.2): the warning icon leads the title, the title asks the question with the connection's name, and the primary button says exactly what happens: 'Sign in only operators'.

Bullets with a bold lead, each a concrete effect with real counts from the server at open time: the customer accounts at its domains (88), the domains that stop routing on product cards and what SSO required then applies to, the product rules that use its domains (DJDL's Access rule, with the licenses it already gave staying), and the console (no role without an SSO rule in Members).

Picking 'Customers and operators' from Customers needs no dialog: it only adds operators. Picking 'Customers' from 'Customers and operators' names the operators who stop signing in through it instead.

With the dialog open the page can't scroll: the dialog is centred in the first viewport on desktop, and on phone it is the bottom sheet (grab handle, primary full width above Cancel). Cancel has focus when it opens.
Pressed, the primary reads 'Saving…' and both buttons are disabled; on an error the dialog stays open with the error inline and the audience is unchanged.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.

Dialog and drawer head (B4): a 3px rule in the origin's accent along the top (none on a destructive or cautious confirmation), a head band with a hairline, one leading glyph or none (severity on a confirmation, the subject's mark on a record, never a service tile), title at or under 20/28; blurred backdrop with a flat fallback under reduced transparency.

findings.issue: Title wrapped on phone; bullets of two clauses.
findings.resolution: Title 'Sign in only operators?'; bullets one clause each; background rebuilt on the new Connection layout; Cancel is an outline button with no first-render focus fill.
